title: Agent Arthur Lyons offers him Broadway
summary: Lyons, a struggling agent, listens at the Nest and asks whether Wooding wants to go downtown, which is what the band was working toward.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You see, so that's the way that went. But, see, I didn't understand in those days what it meant. But I understood later on when towards the end of my days at the club. First place, there was a man, Arthur S. Lyons. He was a fellow -- he was a struggling agent in those days. And he'd come down to the Nest and he'd sit there and he watched the boys and ask for a couple of numbers. Cause anytime we saw a tuxedo or anything like that come in the place, we all got freshed up. Guys would take off, take five out, go wash their face and get all warmed up and get ready for this tuxedo. Cause we knew sooner or later that one was going to be (our out). Because we never intended to stay in the Nest. That was a steppingstone.

So now, when Arthur come in there for a couple of pieces, he was always speak and he got more friendly, and one day he says, "Listen Sam, how would you like to go down on Broadway?" I said, "That 's what I'm trying for." See, because
I'd had two or three good numbers see, I'd made some arrangements on these numbers myself. I'll tell you, you want to know how I started to do this?
